rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes the comment text from 'power of 2' to 'power of 1' on line 119. Comments in C++/CUDA are stripped during compilation and have zero effect on generated machine code. The actual executable code `BLOCK_SIZE = 1 << (int)log2f(BLOCK_SIZE);` is identical in both versions. Since the compiled CUDA kernels are byte-for-byte identical, no input can produce different outputs.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation is in a source code comment within the CUDA kernel string, not in executable code. The mutation tool identified and perturbed the numeric constant '2' in the comment string '// Ensure block size is power of 2 for reduction', changing it to '1'. Comments are completely ignored by the C++ compiler during compilation of the CUDA kernel. Since both the original and mutated code compile to identical GPU machine code, they will always produce identical outputs for any possible input. This is confirmed by Layer 2 testing which found bitwise identical results across 112 diverse test rounds.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation only modifies a comment in the CUDA source code. Comments have no semantic effect on program execution. The compiled kernels are functionally identical, making this mutation impossible to distinguish through any input values or configurations. This is a true semantic equivalent - a 'comment-only' mutation that should be filtered out by the mutation testing framework.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should filter out mutations that only affect comments, string literals used for documentation, or other non-executable code segments. A simple AST-level check could identify that the mutated token resides within a comment node and skip such mutations entirely. This would reduce false 'equivalent mutant' reports and focus testing effort on meaningful code mutations.
